summary: Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1950–1958), Taisho University (~1958–1973), Tsuru University (~1968–1974), and Shizuoka University.

Fumio Matsuda works in religious and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Fumio Ouchi (b. 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed a doctorate in literature at Otani University, where he served as an assistant professor (~1993–2000) and later professor (attested 2014).

Fumio Shoji (b. 1979) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University, where he later served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Fumio Tamamuro (b. 1935) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1954–1964) and taught there from ~1966 to 2006, where his students included Nam-lin Hur.
Futoshi Omae works in Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992) and served as a research assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute of Teaching from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and with Georg Bühler, later teaching at Saint Petersburg (~1900–1941) where he taught Otto Rosenberg and Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov.
Félix Nève (1816–1893) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1840) and Christian Lassen (~1840–1841), before becoming a professor at KU Leuven in 1841.
G. V. Aston specializes in philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy from the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Devasthali (1906–1994) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944) and held posts at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (attested 1944) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi and Ryotai Hatai, later holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies there (1935–1971), alongside posts at Kyushu and Tekko Junior College.
Gail Hinich Sutherland works in religious studies and Indology. Sutherland studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule (b. 1921) works in Indology and linguistics. He was a dictionary sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1951) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at the University of Washington (~1958–1964). He held posts at UC San Diego (~1972–1980) and Princeton University (~1980–2000), and taught Richard Gombrich.

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Calcutta, and University of Allahabad. He held posts at Darbhanga Raj Library, Muir Central College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad.

Gangs zhun specializes in Tibetology. They studied at Hainan College for Nationalities (until 1989) and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Davaa-Ochir earned an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under Hanna Havnevik, and also studied under Lama Byambaa.

Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Lycée Thiers and under Jean-Daniel Kieffer (~1817–1828), he served as Professor of Hindustānī at INALCO (~1828–1878) and taught Edward Elbridge Salisbury.

Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (2006) and became an assistant professor at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).
